title: SSE semantic-aware chunking + latency-first flush policy and reconnect token translation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current SSE chunking focuses on fixed byte/token windows which optimizes throughput but often produces mid-sentence flushes increasing client-side latency and downstream parse complexity. Reconnect behavior is tightly coupled to current resume token format, making server rolling upgrades and protocol evolution error-prone for long-lived client connections.

Goal: Implement a server-side semantic-aware chunking mechanism that prefers latency-sensitive flushes at natural boundaries (sentence/paragraph/JSON object end) while still falling back to size/time windows for throughput. Add a reconnect token translation layer to allow resume tokens issued by older runtime versions to be translated or upgraded at reconnect time, enabling rolling upgrades and graceful protocol changes. Maintain backward compatibility with legacy clients that expect length-prefixed or micro-chunk framing.

Scope:
- A server-side "semantic flush" module to annotate and decide chunk boundaries using lightweight heuristics (punctuation, sentence boundary detection, JSON-object closure, and model token stream signals).
- A latency-first flush policy that triggers earlier flushes for short semantic units while allowing a throughput booster when aggregation yields no semantic boundary for longer than a threshold.
- A reconnect token translation shim in the control plane that can decode legacy resume tokens, map them to current stream lineage, and re-issue a modern token or a compatibility resume path.
- A compatibility mode for legacy clients (length-prefixed JSONL and small-chunk clients) to accept both semantic-chunked SSE and legacy framed payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits SSE events at semantic boundaries for >= 80% of sentences in benchmark prompts (configurable threshold)
End-to-end median client perceived latency improves by >= 15% on chat workloads dominated by short replies (<= 40 tokens)
Reconnect token translation successfully resumes 99.9% of sessions that were created with runtime versions from the last 18 months during rolling upgrades
Legacy clients can opt-in to compatibility mode and receive length-prefixed frames without breaking current streaming clients
Automated tests cover chunking decisions, token translation, and compatibility shim behavior in CI
design_decisions: Use a hybrid heuristic combining punctuation, whitespace patterns, JSON/structural closers, and model-provided end-of-turn signals rather than an expensive NLP model on the hot path

Expose two tunable thresholds: latency_threshold_ms (max time to wait for semantic boundary) and size_threshold_tokens (max tokens before forced flush). Default config prioritizes latency for short replies.
Emit a per-event metadata header (sse-semantics: sentence|paragraph|struct|forced) to aid client parsing and analytics
Keep resume token opaque to clients but maintain a control-plane mapping: token_v1 -> canonical_stream_id@offset; translation shim will validate lineage and re-issue token_v2 on reconnect

Compatibility mode will prefix SSE payloads with a short ASCII marker when length-prefixed frames are requested (no change to main streaming behavior, server sends both markers concurrently if requested)
implementation_notes: Hot-path heuristic must be O(1) per token; use a small ring buffer of recent token chars and structural depth counters for JSON/markdown-like structures
Instrument runtime to emit chunk boundary candidate scores for observability (histogram of candidate scores and reasons)
Reconnect translation: add a lightweight control-plane lookup service (cached) that maps legacy tokens and validates session affinity before accepting resume requests
Define a clear incompatibility window: tokens older than 18 months require explicit migration and will be rejected with a helpful error containing migration steps
Add feature flag 'semantic_chunking_v1' to ramp traffic progressively (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with canary groups by customer tier
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Semantic heuristics cause too many small flushes hurting throughput. Mitigation: enforce size_threshold_tokens and backpressure-aware batching when client latency SLAs allow it.

Risk: Resume token translation could introduce security gaps if mapping is naive. Mitigation: require server-side lineage proof (signed metadata) and rate-limit translation attempts; add audit log entries for translations.
Risk: Legacy clients may fail on dual-markered streams. Mitigation: compatibility mode requires explicit opt-in via initial handshake header (X-Redwood-Compat: legacy-length-prefix)
testing_plan: Unit tests for semantic boundary detector covering punctuation, nested JSON, markdown, and edge cases (long no-punctuation sequences)
Load tests comparing throughput/latency trade-offs for semantic vs fixed-window chunking using our chat benchmark suite
Chaos test: simulate rolling upgrade where half the cluster issues v1 tokens and the other half expects v2; validate translation shim correctness and failover behavior
Integration test: legacy client emulator receives length-prefixed frames while new client receives SSE with metadata header; verify both parse payloads correctly
E2E test for reconnect: interrupt streams at random offsets and assert resumed content continuity and idempotency
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge feature-flagged implementation behind semantic_chunking_v1 and token_translation service disabled (dry-run metrics only)
Stage 1: Canary 10% of non-enterprise traffic with translation shim enabled for canary only
Stage 2: Expand to 50% after verifying latency and throughput metrics; enable legacy compatibility opt-in path
Stage 3: Full rollout after 1 week of stable metrics and no token-translation security alerts
Stage 4: Deprecation notice and migration guide for tokens older than 18 months
monitoring_and_slo: Metrics to add: semantic_chunk_ratio, avg_chunk_tokens, median_client_latency_per_chunk, token_translation_success_rate, token_translation_latency
Set SLO: token_translation_success_rate >= 99.9% and token_translation_latency p95 < 200ms
Add alert: semantic_chunk_ratio drops > 20% from baseline or median_client_latency regresses > 10%
Emit tracing spans for translate_token and boundary_decision to surface in the Console
